issue_context.title: Insteon - aiohttp timeout error during test connection
comments:
Hey there @teharris1, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`insteon`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L202) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

@daaustintx a patch was put into 0.113.0 (not released yet) that may (or may not) fix this issue. I cannot recreate this issue but there is another underlying issue that has come up which is related. I you would not mind testing when 0.113.0 is released that would be great.

Thanks. Unfortunately, logs are not going to help. What is happening here is the TCP connection between HA and the Hub is not being released correctly on the Hub side so the Hub thinks the connection is still there. The Hub only allows one client to connect at a time. It is a really bad design. When the TCP connection is still open the next attempt fails. For some reason, the Hub never closes the connection on its side and so HA can never reconnect. When you restart the Hub the connection, of course, is closed allowing HA to connect again. It is an inherent issue with the Hub. I have tried a lot of things to force the connection to close but to no avail. I will keep trying to make it better and I appreciate your help.

@teharris1 Thank you for the feedback. Your reply summarized an overall issue with insteon hubs that i kept experiencing since integrating into HASS. 

**As a test**
I purchased an Insteon USB interface and connected it to my VM that's running HASS. Since transitioning to the USB interface, i've not had any disconnection issues. Also, a lot of small issues disappeared such as device responsive time. 

**To anyone who's having any odd issues with HASS and the Insteon Hub.** 
Save your time, blood pressure and state of mind by purchasing an insteon USB interface (USB Stick/USB Dual-Band Adapter). After transitioning to a USB interface, I've not had any issues and have not had to stress about rebooting the hub or HASS entirely. 

**A few things to consider**
(1) I am able to confirm devices are able to interact with both Insteon Hub and USB Interface. You may not immediately find this information online
(2) If purchasing the Insteon USB Stick, you may want to purchase the range extender. The USB stick is RF ONLY and not Powerline. The range extender is Dual-band (RF / Powerline) which is beneficial to devices that are only Powerline or not in near range of the USB Stick.
(3) After the transition, i still noticed small odd behavior. However, I factory restore each Insteon device and first paired it to HASS. After confirming the device interacts with HASS, I paired it to the Insteon Hub and pushed all software base changes. For example, I have a few rooms with a Keypad and Ceiling Fan Controller(FanLinc). First, I removed both devices from the Insteon Hub. Then, I paired both devices to HASS and confirmed they worked. After successfully confirming HASS interactions, I paired both devices to the Insteon Hub and created four seasons for the Ceiling Fan speeds (Off, Low, Med, High). Now, I am able to control the Keypad and Celling Fan from HASS and Insteon Hub. 
(4) You no longer need to configure HASS with Insteon's Hub if using a different computer interface. Please make sure to change your settings to only allow the computer interface. 
(5) If using the In-wall Keypad, you MUST pair each button to HASS as a controller and Responder
(6) FanLinc is ONLY a responder and can not control devices meaning changes on the FanLinc itself will not reflect in HASS. I had to write a python automation script to acknowledge changes from the Keypad to HASS that reflects in Homekit.

There hasn't been any activity on this issue recently. Due to the high number of incoming GitHub notifications, we have to clean some of the old issues, as many of them have already been resolved with the latest updates.
Please make sure to update to the latest Home Assistant version and check if that solves the issue. Let us know if that works for you by adding a comment 👍
This issue has now been marked as stale and will be closed if no further activity occurs. Thank you for your contributions.

review_comments: We cannot do this. This will block startup of ALL of Home Assistant. To implement this, convert it to a config entry and raise `ConfigEntryNotReady` from `async_setup_entry` and HA will take care of this.

Ugh, OK, then we cannot do that. I have a PR open to add config flow. I was going to add retries to that ticket but it was going to take longer. I am going to close this PR and fix the issue there. I will look for ConfigEntryNotReady examples in other code to understand what you are saying.
